mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for 3 consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 4% for 3 consecutive months signals accommodative policy, lowering discount rates and boosting equity present value, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) above 1.5% of GDP for 3 consecutive months reduces aggregate demand, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 1.5% of GDP for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in expansionary periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) below 1% of GDP for 3 consecutive months signals contractionary policy, raising discount rates and compressing equity present value, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 1% of GDP for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in contractionary periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% of GDP for 3 consecutive months indicates expanding domestic demand, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 2% of GDP for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in expansionary periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 1.5% of GDP for 3 consecutive months signals softening demand or supply constraints, compressing equity present value, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 1.5% of GDP for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in soft landing/contractionary periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% for 3 consecutive months indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy, compressing discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in inflation periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5.5% for 3 consecutive months signals a deep recession, reducing equity risk and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in recession periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
